summary: Developed by the Anka Pioneers team from Anka Bilim Koleji for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, "Space Pioneers" is a Unity and C#-based educational game designed to enhance the comprehensibility of disconnected and abstract theoretical lessons in Aerospace Sciences. Featuring four core missions—station docking and fuel budgeting, collecting space debris for sustainable space, sending a telescope to the Sun's orbit via Kepler's laws and orbital mechanics, and communicating with the ground station—the project allows students to learn by doing rather than memorizing, utilizing physics mechanics built on NASA data and helpful in-game hints.
details:
Project Report: Space Pioneers

1. Project Profile

  • Project Name: Space Pioneers
  • Developing Team / Institution: Anka Pioneers / Anka Bilim Koleji (NASA Space Apps Challenge)
  • Core Motto: "Learn by doing, not by memorizing!"

2. Problem Definition

  • Theoretical lessons in technical disciplines such as Aerospace Sciences are often disconnected and insufficiently demonstrated practically, making them difficult for students to fully understand.
  • Research indicates that supporting theoretical lessons with practical examples increases exam performance by an average of 6% and reduces course failure rates by 1.5 times (University of Washington, 2014).

3. Purpose of the Project

  • To transform abstract and disconnected theoretical lessons into tangible and understandable concepts through gamification.
  • To enable students to comprehend space and aviation sciences by experiencing them in an interactive environment.

4. Solution and Game Missions

  • Developed within the scope of the project, the Unity-based gamefeatures hint buttons that allow players to both have fun and grasp the underlying concepts and lessons. The game consists of 4 core missions in total:
    • Mission 1: Docking to the Station and Fuel Budget
    • Mission 2: Collecting Space Debris and Sustainable Space
    • Mission 3: Sending a Telescope to the Sun's Orbit, Kepler's Law, and Orbital Mechanics
    • Mission 4: Telecommunication and Communication with the Ground Station

5. Methodology and Technologies

  • Team Organization: The project team is divided into 4 main groups: software, design, game testing, and report writing.
  • Software Infrastructure: The game was developed using the Unity engine and the C# programming language.
  • Visual and Physics Modeling: Designs and animations were created using Blender alongside NASA's 3D models, while the game's physics mechanics were built directly using data obtained from NASA.

6. Impact Area and Future Goals

  • In addition to increasing the comprehensibility of Aerospace Sciences theories, it provides an educational platform that appeals not only to specialized students but to all educational groups.
  • Future plans include adding a multiplayer mode to reflect the complexities of space systems and mission strategy planning in a multi-user environment.
